title: SpaceX Launches 24 Starlink Satellites From California in 90th Falcon 9 Mission of 2026
excerpt: SpaceX deployed another batch of Starlink V2 Mini satellites from Vandenberg Space Force Base as the company pushes past 10,800 satellites in orbit and maintains its record-setting launch cadence.
body:
• SpaceX launched 24 Starlink V2 Mini satellites from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on the Starlink 17-38 mission on August 8.
  • The Falcon 9's first-stage booster successfully landed on the droneship "Of Course I Still Love You" in the Pacific Ocean.
  • SpaceX now has more than 10,800 Starlink satellites in orbit, with the constellation handling over 4 million subscribers worldwide.
  • This was approximately the 90th Falcon 9 launch of 2026, keeping SpaceX on pace to break its own annual launch record.

SpaceX launched 24 Starlink broadband internet satellites into low-Earth orbit from California on Saturday, continuing its relentless launch cadence as the company builds out the world's largest satellite constellation.

The Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Space Launch Complex 4 East at Vandenberg Space Force Base in Santa Barbara County during a launch window that opened at 7 a.m. PT. The mission, designated Starlink 17-38, deployed 24 V2 Mini satellites into a sun-synchronous polar orbit about an hour after liftoff.

Booster Recovery and Reusability Milestones

As has become routine for SpaceX, the Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the upper stage roughly two and a half minutes after launch, flipped around and performed a series of engine burns to guide itself back to a controlled landing on the droneship "Of Course I Still Love You," stationed in the Pacific Ocean.

https://x.com/SpaceX/status/2086160265553334635

SpaceX's drone ship fleet has now accumulated more than 640 successful orbital booster landings. The company's aggressive reuse program — with some boosters flying more than 25 times — has fundamentally reduced the cost of reaching orbit and enabled the high launch frequency that underpins the Starlink business model.

The two-stage, 230-foot Falcon 9 has become the world's most active orbital rocket. With this launch, SpaceX has conducted approximately 90 Falcon rocket launches in 2026, including one Falcon Heavy mission, keeping the company on pace to surpass last year's record of over 130 orbital flights.

Constellation Growth

The Starlink constellation now exceeds 10,800 satellites in orbit, according to Spaceflight Now, making it by far the largest satellite network ever assembled. The 17-38 mission added another batch of V2 Mini Optimized satellites — the latest generation of Starlink hardware, which offers improved bandwidth and coverage compared to earlier versions.

"The Falcon 9's first-stage booster successfully landed on the droneship "Of Course I Still Love You" in the Pacific Ocean."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=HOTEJM2cvl0

SpaceX has launched at least 69 batches of V2 Mini Optimized satellites this year alone, with missions departing from both Vandenberg in California and Cape Canaveral in Florida at a pace of roughly one every four to five days.

Starlink now serves over 4 million subscribers across more than 100 countries and territories, positioning it as a major player in global broadband connectivity, particularly in underserved and rural markets.

Regulatory Landscape in Key Markets

While Starlink has rapidly expanded across North America, Europe and parts of Asia-Pacific, its entry into India — the world's second-largest internet market — remains pending. Indian regulators have been cautious about approving Starlink's satellite broadband service, with ongoing discussions between SpaceX and India's Department of Telecommunications over licensing, spectrum allocation and data localisation requirements.

For Indian diaspora communities, particularly those in rural or remote areas of countries where Starlink already operates, the service has emerged as a viable alternative to traditional broadband, offering download speeds typically between 50 and 200 Mbps with latency under 40 milliseconds.
